🇲🇽🏠 <u>Housing Registrations Up 200%, Driven by Vivienda para el Bienestar</u>

New housing projects registered in Mexico jumped 200% in the first half of 2026 versus the first half of 2022, according to BBVA Research via El Economista, pushed mainly by the social-housing segment tied to Sheinbaum's Vivienda para el Bienestar.

By June the national housing registry counted 389,000 homes in production and unsold, up 84.6% in a year. The bottleneck: 154,000 of them (39.6%) show no progress or less than 20%. The program already has 667,000 homes under contract, 37% of its 1.8 million goal.

"It's not an easy task; a goal of 1.8 million homes is a lot... we should be a little patient," said Samuel Vázquez, BBVA Research's chief economist for Mexico.

🇲🇽✊ <u>282,000 IMSS Workers Vote by Secret Ballot, and Say No to 6.8%</u>

Mexico's Social Security (IMSS) workers voted on their own contract raise on October 14, in a secret-ballot consultation supervised by the Federal Labor Conciliation and Registration Center. About 282,000 took part, close to 60% of those eligible, at 670 polling stations.

The offer, 2.9% on base pay plus 3.9% in benefits, lost. "The results are clear. The majority of those who participated decided not to approve the salary proposal," said SNTSS union leader Rafael Olivos, who now goes back to the table with IMSS.

Before the 2019 labor reform, union bosses signed these deals behind closed doors.
banner: IMSS WORKERS VOTE NO ON 6.8% RAISE

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PRI's Political Police Kept a File on El Universal's Owner</u>

Reports from the Federal Security Directorate (DFS), the PRI regime's political police, show it spied on Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, director of El Universal, in the mid-1980s.

The agents' verdict: he spent little time on journalism and a lot on "gestoría ante la administración pública", lobbying the government for his other businesses. The DFS filed El Universal as critical of the government but a "defender of business groups," and went through his correspondence too.

Ealy Ortiz still runs El Universal.
banner: DFS FILE: EL UNIVERSAL'S OWNER SPIED ON

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court: Five Votes Are Enough to Force a Congress to Do Its Job</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court ruled that a simple majority, five of nine justices, is now enough to declare that a state congress failed to legislate and order it to fix that. The old bar was six.

First case: Quintana Roo's legislature never set rules guaranteeing that people with disabilities can run for municipal office. Now it has to consult them and pass the law before the legal cutoff for changing election rules ahead of 2030.

Justice Loretta Ortiz Ahlf cast the deciding vote, 5–4.
banner: SUPREME COURT: 5 VOTES TO FORCE A LAW

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico's Foreign Minister to the Senate: Sovereignty Is Not on the Table</u>

Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco, reporting to the Senate on Sheinbaum's second year in office, laid down the line: "sovereignty and national interest are not negotiated, not limited, and not subordinated to anyone."

The receipts: Mexico's consulates made 9,632 visits to US migrant detention centers this year, 36 a day, and handled 152,466 protection cases. Monthly fentanyl seizures at the US southern border are down 67%, by US Customs and Border Protection's own count.

"For a country whose history is marked by invasions and foreign interventions, international law is our principal weapon."

🇲🇽💵 <u>IMF to Mexico: Tax Homes, Cut Fuel Subsidies, "Target" Welfare</u>

The IMF wants Mexico to "consider more ambitious and accelerated consolidation," El Economista reports: phase out fuel subsidies, raise property and vehicle taxes, end border tax incentives, and "better target" social programs that reach 43 million Mexicans for 1.06 trillion pesos, 2.6% of GDP. It's the same Washington recipe that gave Latin America its lost decade in the 1980s.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Edomex: 35 Women-Only Clinics, Abandoned Hospitals Finished</u>

The State of Mexico will open 35 medical units exclusively for women under Mujeres con Bienestar, and finish hospitals left abandoned in Ecatepec, Chimalhuacán, Nezahualcóyotl, Tlalnepantla, Zinacantepec and Aculco, Horacio Duarte told the state legislature. Delfina Gómez and Sheinbaum are funding it together, in the same state where the PRI ruled for nearly a century.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Navy Intelligence Takes Down "Cromo" of the Isthmus</u>

Mexico's Navy intelligence unit and the CNI captured Iván Sánchez Santiago, "Cromo," in Jalisco. He is the alleged head of Los Cromos, a CJNG-linked cell named as a main source of violence in Oaxaca's Isthmus of Tehuantepec. The arrest follows the September 23 detention of Juchitán's sitting mayor, Miguel Sánchez Altamirano, under Operación Sable, which has put more than 250 people behind bars in 11 months.

🇲🇽📉 <u>Mexico City: 748,000 People Out of Poverty</u>

Between 2020 and 2025, 748,000 people in Mexico City escaped poverty by unmet basic needs and more than half a million left extreme poverty, Clara Brugada told the city Congress. That's measured by Evalúa CDMX, a stricter yardstick than Coneval. Her welfare network now reaches 2.6 million people, and public care services (community kitchens, laundries, day-care) have freed 308,000 hours of unpaid domestic work.

🇲🇽🔍 <u>16,414 Missing People Found, Experts Brought In to Audit the Registry</u>

Mexico's Interior Ministry reports 16,414 people located under the National Search Strategy: 6,939 through the Unified Identity Platform, 4,788 with the states, 3,473 via immediate search alerts and 1,214 in field searches. Rosa Icela Rodríguez is bringing in specialists from USC, Maryland, UNAM, ITAM and CIESAS to analyze the national registry and clean up its data.
